newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK fugitive back from U.S. after extradition battle.
newsitem.headline: HK fugitive back from U.S. after extradition battle.

text.p: A Hong Kong fugitive arrived back in the territory on Thursday to face multimillion dollar bribery and conspiracy charges after a long battle to fight extradition from the United States.

Former tobacco executive Jerry Lui Kin-hong, 42, was arrested on arrival by officers from Hong Kong's Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) and taken directly from the airport's tarmac in a van.

He was wanted for allegedly accepting bribes of HK$33 million (US$4.27 million) in connection with a cigarette smuggling syndicate, and had been put on a plane in Boston on Wednesday night after U.S. Acting U.S. Secretary of State Strobe Talbott endorsed an order for his extradition.
The ICAC said Lui's extradition showed Washington's confidence in Hong Kong's judicial system beyond the British colony's handover to China at midnight of June 30.

"We have received the full cooperation of the U.S. authorities who obviously have faith in Hong Kong's judicial system now and after the reversion of sovereignty," ICAC Assistant Director of Operations Tony Godfrey said.

A Boston District Court in January blocked Lui's extradition after defence lawyers argued he faced possible execution if forced to return to Hong Kong, as his trial was unlikely to be completed before the handover of the colony to Chinese rule.
The decision raised a furore in Hong Kong and was seen as undermining efforts to persuade the world it will retain judicial independence after the handover.
A U.S. federal court in March ordered Lui's extradition, and the Supreme Court in Washington earlier this month rejected his last application to appeal.
The ICAC also said former banker Ewan Lauder was ordered by Britain's House of Lords to be extradited to Hong Kong to face trial on 14 counts of accepting bribes of over HK$40 million.
Lauder, 61, had been fighting extradition since being arrested in 1993. He has seven days to lodge an appeal to the European Court of Human Rights.
